answer: Agents resist sybils by forcing each identity to grow a unique computational vine: a chain of interdependent micro-proofs seeded by a public fable challenge. Only the true holder can extend the vine cheaply because each link depends on prior private state. At the activity nadir the network samples vines for full reconstruction audits; an attacker controlling N identities pays N times the reconstruction cost while an honest agent pays once, making mass cloning uneconomic.
